title: Apple's 'The Morning Show' To End With Season 5 in 2027
excerpt: Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon confirmed the Emmy-winning series will conclude with its fifth and final season, premiering next year on Apple TV+.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Apple TV+ confirms Season 5 of 'The Morning Show' will premiere in 2027 as the series' final season.
  • Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon return, joined by new cast members including Jeff Daniels and Reneé Rapp.
  • The show debuted in 2019 and became Apple TV+'s most-watched series, tackling significant social issues.
  • Showrunner Charlotte Stoudt promises a thoughtful conclusion to the characters' journeys in the final season.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=C2gCQYJ3l9c

Apple TV+ confirmed on Thursday that The Morning Show, the streamer's flagship drama starring Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon, will end with its fifth season. The final run is set to premiere in 2027.

The announcement closes the book on one of Apple's tentpole originals — a series that debuted alongside the streaming platform itself in November 2019 and grew into its most-watched show. Over four seasons, the drama about the inner workings of a network morning news program has tackled sexual misconduct, pandemic-era chaos, tech-industry power plays and press freedom, earning multiple Emmy nominations along the way.

A Farewell Crafted 'With Intentionality'

Aniston, 57, who stars as anchor Alex Levy and serves as executive producer, said the creative team knew going in that Season 5 would be the end.

https://x.com/NexusPointNews/status/2080344416858816975

"Going in knowing it would be our last, we were so fortunate to craft the conclusion with intentionality, and honor these characters the way they deserve."

— Jennifer Aniston, star and executive producer

Aniston added that Apple had supported the show's vision "from the beginning," and called the experience of working with the cast and crew a privilege. "We've become such a family, and we're all so excited to share this final season," she said.

Witherspoon, 50, who plays reporter Bradley Jackson, described her nine years on the series as "the honor of a lifetime." The actress and executive producer framed the show as more than a workplace drama.

"This was always more than a show about a newsroom — it was a show about why the newsroom matters. About freedom of the press, and the journalists who protect the fourth estate, often at great cost."

— Reese Witherspoon, star and executive producer

Star-Studded Final Season Cast

The final season brings back the show's core ensemble: Billy Crudup, who won Apple TV+'s first Emmy in 2020 for his role as network executive Cory Ellison, returns alongside Mark Duplass, Nestor Carbonell, Karen Pittman, Nicole Beharie and Jon Hamm.

Apple also unveiled a roster of new additions. Jeff Daniels — who previously anchored HBO's newsroom drama The Newsroom — will play Lukas, a self-made billionaire and investment firm founder. Reneé Rapp has been cast as Samantha, a rising star in the UBN news team, in what marks her return to acting after focusing on her music career. Jesse Williams, Sean Hayes and Lizzy Caplan round out the announced newcomers, with more casting expected.

Where Season 5 Picks Up

A Star-Studded Farewell
›Returning Cast: Jennifer Aniston, Reese Witherspoon, Billy Crudup, Mark Duplass, Nestor Carbonell.
›New Additions: Jeff Daniels, Reneé Rapp, Jesse Williams, Sean Hayes, Lizzy Caplan.
›Aniston describes the final season as crafted 'with intentionality'.
›Witherspoon calls her role an 'honor of a lifetime'.

Season 4, which premiered in September 2025, ended on a series of dramatic cliffhangers, including Bradley's detention in Belarus and the exposure of a UBN executive involved in a cover-up. Showrunner Charlotte Stoudt has previously teased that Season 5 will dig into the unresolved relationship between Bradley and Crudup's Cory Ellison.

In a statement accompanying the announcement, Stoudt offered a broader preview: "For five seasons, these messy, resilient journalists have chased their dreams. Now we'll see where their endeavors lead them — what story will they ultimately choose for themselves."

Apple TV+'s Flagship Signs Off

The Morning Show holds a unique place in Apple's streaming strategy. It was among the first batch of originals that launched Apple TV+ in fall 2019 and has remained a marquee title as the platform expanded its library. According to Deadline, the series broke viewership records after its third season and became Apple TV+'s most-watched show — a distinction it held through Season 4.

The show's end comes as Apple continues to invest in prestige drama but has also trimmed some titles from its roster. Earlier this year, the streamer cancelled the Emmy-nominated Palm Royale after two seasons. The Morning Show will be one of Apple TV+'s longest-running original series when it concludes.

The Morning Show's Impact
›Launched in November 2019 as Apple TV+'s first original show.
›Became the most-watched series on Apple TV+.
›Tackled issues like sexual misconduct and press freedom.
›Earned multiple Emmy nominations throughout its run.

For diaspora audiences who followed Hasan Minhaj's guest arc in Season 2 and the show's recurring exploration of media representation, the final season offers one last chapter in a series that consistently engaged with questions about whose stories get told — and who gets to tell them.

Season 5 of The Morning Show will premiere on Apple TV+ in 2027. A specific date has not been announced.
